doc.title: Abe Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Photographs, his first album with Hank Jones, and Abe Most Day
summary: He shows photos, describes the album with Hank Jones and Martha Tilton, and mentions his City Hall day.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Can you tell me about the pictures you brought.
Oh yes. You want me to hold this up? You want to do it later?
Yeah, well we’ve already taken a shot of them, so.

Oh good. This is the very first album I decided to start recording after all this, my playing at Fox and stuff. so this is myself of course and Monty Budwig, Jake Hanna, Sam was only on the one date, and Hank Jones. And Hank just fell right in. He says, “Oh, that’s what you want to do.” Because what I did, the first tune was — and that’s what set the whole thing up – “These Foolish Things” I think. He says — I just played the melody. And he says, “Oh that’s what you want.” He thought it was going to be bebop and all that stuff. Just play and let’s play for the people. So after that he knew exactly what we should do. So this is that. When I had the big band I decided to go after the best which was Martha Tilton and unfortunately the mic is in her face but that’s me on the side playing with the big band when she was singing “Angels Sing” or something like that. These are, a friend of mine put these together for me, it shows, like a little background of my, everything that I’ve done. This one is I went to a Staples and they did this picture from something I had on the wall and this is Tommy Dorsey and I’m fixing my plastic reed there. I say plastic things. People say, “Why do you tell them you play plastic?” I don’t care. I used to when I first got with them, the new reeds, I heard somebody when I left the stand, “He sounds just like an oboe.” I said oh, I don’t think I sound like an oboe. But anyway those are all I brought. If you want me to send any more, I mean if I can find some.
Yeah, I’d love to have some.

I’ll see what I’ve got. And that’s just a thing we did, this one — Zan Stewart is one of the local writers who loves music and this is just an article about — well this is Frank Morocco. See I’m back to accordion. This is a great accordionist and Jake Hanna and even Sam Most. When we get around to doing it, this is what we work with.
So you had an Abe Most Day in Los Angeles, did you?
You know something? The Abe Most Day is, I forgot what day it is, but they’ve already made a day for me. Did you know that?
Oh you did. Yeah. I don’t remember what day it was but I had a City Hall, Abe Most Day, yeah it was something.

Well when you get old enough I guess, these things start coming and you don’t really — by then, I wouldn’t say who cares but, you know, they’re nice to have. And any of these other honors, which I appreciate you know. But I just like to play and hopefully the people like it.
